candidate_ledger.label: Reincarnator initial copying extent within printed documentary conditional
candidate_ledger.decision: accept bounded literal-question precision extension; documentary scope gap only
candidate_ledger.native_region: Power paragraph final two sentences, parenthetical copying scope followed by loss consequence
candidate_ledger.exact_quote: Aliens with the power to copy your power may do so (copying both your Reincarnator power and whatever power you are reincarnated as), but if they lose an encounter while doing so they must reincarnate, losing their original power.
candidate_ledger.current_literal_clause: what happens when another power copies this one and then loses
candidate_ledger.actual_scope_rationale: The current question supplies copying as part of the condition and expressly asks the consequence of subsequent loss. A source-correct answer that says the copier reincarnates and loses its original power answers that clause without identifying whether initial copying includes the current incarnation. The printed initial copying-extent parenthesis is a distinct documentary assertion rather than merely an arithmetic or cosmetic rendering of the asked loss consequence.
candidate_ledger.semantic_alternative_rejected: Broad what happens language could conversationally invite the whole conditional, but that is insufficient to require this initial extent as an independently demanded material fact under the strict literal-scope rule.
candidate_ledger.proposed_bounded_extension: Under the original printed copying conditional, does the copier copy Reincarnator alone or both it and the current incarnation, and what happens when that copier loses?
candidate_ledger.required_documentary_answer: It may copy both Reincarnator and the current incarnation; if it loses while doing so, it reincarnates and loses its original power.
